goal: Three agents on wearables, office and automotive, under the tier quota, each seeded with a ranked candidate list of contested devices and the specific tier error most likely in that domain.
outcome: All three completed — the first wave since wave 1 where no agent was killed.
findings: The tier quota held across a full wave: 10 of 15 records above D0, against 3 of 17 two waves ago. It is not a one-run effect.

Two pairs were produced deliberately, which is now what SCOUT asks for. grizzl-e-classic (D0) and grizzl-e-classic-connect (D2) are the same EV charger body about $50 apart, differing only in whether there is a radio inside. prusa-mk4s and bambu-lab-a1 both land at D2 by different routes, which is a useful answer for a reader who assumed one of them was disqualifying.

Agents declined records for the right reasons and said so. Office dropped the Rigol DP832 because its LAN interface is a $140 add-on rather than standard, making the base SKU a D0 restating a fact the catalog already had, and dropped a second audio recorder with the same optional-Bluetooth story as the Zoom. That is the tier quota working without those specific devices being named.

The Bambu record is the clearest case yet of judging documentation over reputation. There is a great deal of coverage of the January 2025 authorisation-control firmware dispute and comparatively little documentation; the agent went to Bambu's current wiki, found SD-card printing bypasses the cloud and LAN Only plus Developer Mode still opens local MQTT/FTP with no account, and filed D2.

system_gaps_found.gap: siglent-spd3303x was filed D1 with its own radios field reading ['none']. D1 means a radio exists and still has nowhere to phone home; no radio and no vendor cloud is D0. An Ethernet port is not a radio.
system_gaps_found.fix: Corrected to D0, and validate.mjs now fails any D1 without a radio. This matters beyond one record: a tier quota gives agents a standing incentive to classify upward, and this is what that drift looks like when it is honest rather than dishonest — a defensible-sounding reason to call something more contested than it was. The incentive the quota creates is now checked mechanically.

system_gaps_found.gap: The ladder's D0 test ('no intentional radiator') is a proxy for 'cannot reach its maker', and two device classes break the proxy in opposite directions — a GMRS transceiver that transmits by design with no vendor behind it at all, and a PoE camera or Ethernet UPS that holds no radio grant and talks to its maker all day.
system_gaps_found.fix: Both written into PRINCIPLES as explicit carve-outs, with the note that the sibling-control heuristic does not apply to Part 95/80 voice radios because a grant is expected there. The new D1 validator rule deliberately does not check D2/D3 for this reason.

system_gaps_found.gap: Two wearables records cited a DuckDuckGo results page routed through a text-extraction proxy as a source, while working around the exhausted search budget. A results page has no stable content and a proxied one has weaker provenance still.
system_gaps_found.fix: Both replaced or removed; Polar's own support page carries the firmware claim verbatim. validate.mjs now rejects search engines and extraction proxies as source URLs, deliberately allowing fccid.io/search.php?q=... because for an absence-of-grant finding the search IS the evidence. The first version of that rule broke nine legitimate records before being narrowed.

system_gaps_found.gap: Fourth radios enum gap. ANT+ was being carried as 'unknown' or folded into ble, though it is an open published standard any compatible watch can receive with no vendor pairing — a different fact about who can read your data than Bluetooth.
system_gaps_found.fix: Added ant_plus; tagged two new records and backfilled garmin-hrm-200. Also added two_way_radio for licensed voice transceivers in the same wave.

honest_limitations: The Cressi Leonardo was abandoned after roughly ten fetch attempts — cressi.com serves a broken TLS certificate and every retailer mirror tried returned 403, 404 or a DNS failure. It would have been the D0 contrast to the Shearwater D2 and is still worth having.

The session's WebSearch budget was exhausted before this wave began, and it shaped the output: one agent lost a record to fetch failures alone, and another produced the proxy citations described above. Seeded candidate lists mitigate this but do not replace search.

Bambu Lab is a live vendor-ledger candidate that all of this leaves unscored. The January 2025 dispute is dated and well covered; the agent correctly declined to score the vendor itself and left the record at 0.

Records were reviewed for schema, source class, tier/radio consistency, hedged deciding facts and citation quality. Two deciding facts were independently re-verified by the orchestrator (Grizzl-E Classic Connect, Polar H10); the other thirteen were not re-derived from primary sources.
surprises: The tier quota's own failure mode showed up in the same wave that proved the quota works. Told to produce contested records, an agent found a defensible reason to call a radio-free bench supply D1. Nothing about that was dishonest — the reasoning was written out plainly enough for a reviewer to catch it — but it is a reminder that every incentive this project adds to the briefs needs a corresponding check in the validator, or it will quietly bend the catalog.
